sources.entry: Knopo - Native macOS outliner for local-first notes stored as plain Markdown files. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/alkalim/Knopo) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: Knopo is a native macOS (AppKit/SwiftUI, no Electron) outliner for Logseq-style block notes stored as plain Markdown files in a local folder.
summary.what_it_does: It treats each note as a block in a tree, with pages made of nested blocks, and saves everything as .md files in a graph folder that the user owns. Each block maps to a line in its file, and untouched blocks re-serialize byte-for-byte, so files are not rewritten unnecessarily. It supports page links [[Page]], block references ((id)), embeds {{embed}}, #tags, and read-only {{query}} filters combining tags, page references, task state, and properties with and/or/not. A rebuildable SQLite index (.knopo/cache.db) powers full-text search (⌘K), find (⌘F), backlinks, and tag views. It also includes a journal view, GitHub-style pipe tables, a right sidebar for side-by-side cards, and multiple windows or tabs with several graphs open.
use_cases: Keep daily journal and personal notes as Markdown files
Outline and organize ideas as nested blocks
Link notes together with wiki-style page links and backlinks
Search across a folder of Markdown notes on a Mac
Run live queries over tagged or task blocks in notes
Keep notes in a git-tracked plain-text folder
notable: Plain Markdown source of truth with byte-stable round-tripping, so editing does not churn files
Native AppKit text editing rather than a web-based editor
Rebuildable SQLite index in .knopo/ that is safe to delete
Closed, read-only query filter language for live result lists
Multiple graphs open at once in native windows or tabs, kept in sync
caveats: macOS only; no Windows or Linux support
Early stage; on-disk conventions may still change
Downloaded builds are not notarized and need a Gatekeeper workaround; the app icon step in build-app.sh needs Xcode
